newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada calls to ignore Clyde defence.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada calls to ignore Clyde defence.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources urged shareholders of takeover target Clyde Petroleum to ignore their company's defence on valuation and accept Gulf Canada's takeover offer.
Gulf Canada has launched a 432 million stg takeover for Clyde with a cash offer of 105 pence per share.
Clyde had criticised the offer saying Gulf Canada's approach of valuing the firm on net asset value was not appropriate and should have used cash flow multiples as the true method of valuation.
Gulf Canada said on Wednesday that Clyde's analysis was "fundamentally flawed" and valuation on historic cash flow multiples were "clearly irrelevant".
Gulf reiterated its valuation saying oil and gas firms were valued primarily on expected future cash flows.
"The most appropriate valuation methodology is therefore 'net asset value' which represents the present value of Clyde's projected future cash flows," it said.
Gulf said its offer was 40 percent over Clyde's net asset value of 75 pence as calculated by Clyde's own broker ABN Amro Hoare Govett in its research report dated December 16, 1996.
Clyde Petroleum held firm at 117-1/2 pence in low volume trade of 5,319 shares at 0817 gmt on Wednesday.
